proof:
Source: step 1 (parent G0) of the supplied proof of second_fundamental_form_chart_formula. There Π(A) = A(A*A)⁻¹A* is the orthogonal projection onto range A for injective A, and Π is smooth on the open set of injective maps. Only differentiability at an injective point is used, and that is what is proved here.
Notation: ℝ^d := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) (= Rn d); L(X, Y) := (X →L[ℝ] Y) with the operator norm; for a linear map B, range B := LinearMap.range B.toLinearMap and K.starProjection is the orthogonal projection of the ambient space onto the subspace K. For B ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ) let B* ∈ L(ℝᴺ, ℝⁿ) be its adjoint (⟨B*w, v⟩ = ⟨w, Bv⟩; Mathlib ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint). Let G(B) := B* ∘ B ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ) be the Gram operator. Let Ring.inverse be inversion in the Banach algebra L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ), whose multiplication is composition: it is the inverse on units and 0 elsewhere. Put F(B) := B ∘ (Ring.inverse(G(B)) ∘ B*) ∈ L(ℝᴺ, ℝᴺ). Fix an injective A ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ).
1. (The adjoint is a continuous real-linear map.) The map adj : L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ) → L(ℝᴺ, ℝⁿ), B ↦ B*, is additive and satisfies (cB)* = c B* for c ∈ ℝ, because complex conjugation is trivial on ℝ. It is an isometry (‖B*‖ = ‖B‖), hence continuous. So adj is a continuous ℝ-linear map and is differentiable everywhere, with derivative adj itself. [Lean: Mathlib's ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint is only conjugate-linear (≃ₗᵢ⋆[ℝ]), so build the ℝ-CLM as ⟨{toFun := fun B ↦ ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint B, map_add' := by simp, map_smul' := by simp}, ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint.continuous⟩.]
2. (G(A) is a unit.) If G(A)v = 0, then 0 = ⟨A*Av, v⟩ = ⟨Av, Av⟩ = ‖Av‖², so Av = 0 and v = 0 because A is injective. Thus G(A) is an injective linear endomorphism of the finite-dimensional space ℝⁿ, hence bijective. Its linear inverse is continuous because ℝⁿ is finite-dimensional. So G(A) has a two-sided inverse in L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ), i.e. IsUnit (G(A)). [Lean: ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint_comp_self_injective_iff gives injectivity, since ⇑(A† ∘L A) is definitionally ⇑A† ∘ ⇑A. Then LinearEquiv.ofInjectiveEndo, LinearEquiv.toContinuousLinearEquiv and (ContinuousLinearEquiv.unitsEquiv ℝ (Rn n)).symm produce the unit.]
3. (Invertibility persists near A.) The map B ↦ G(B) = adj(B) ∘ B is continuous: adj is continuous and composition of operators is continuous. The units of the complete normed ring L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ) form an open set (Units.isOpen). Hence S := {B ∈ L(ℝⁿ, ℝᴺ) : G(B) is a unit} is open, contains A by step 2, and so is a neighbourhood of A.
4. (Explicit formula on S.) Let B ∈ S and H := Ring.inverse(G(B)). Then G(B) ∘ H = id (Ring.mul_inverse_cancel). Fix w ∈ ℝᴺ and put p := F(B)w = B(H(B*w)), so p ∈ range B. Let u ∈ range B, say u = Bv. Then ⟨w − p, Bv⟩ = ⟨B*(w − p), v⟩ = ⟨B*w − G(B)(H(B*w)), v⟩ = ⟨B*w − B*w, v⟩ = 0. So p ∈ range B and w − p ⊥ range B. By the characterisation of orthogonal projection (Submodule.eq_starProjection_of_mem_of_inner_eq_zero), Πr(B)w = p = F(B)w. As w is arbitrary, Πr(B) = F(B) for every B ∈ S.
5. (F is differentiable at A.) The identity B ↦ B is differentiable, and B ↦ B* is differentiable by step 1. Hence B ↦ G(B) = adj(B) ∘ B is differentiable at A, since a composition of operator-valued maps differentiable at A is differentiable at A (DifferentiableAt.clm_comp). Ring.inverse is differentiable at the unit G(A) (differentiableAt_inverse; its derivative is T ↦ −G(A)⁻¹ T G(A)⁻¹). By the chain rule, B ↦ Ring.inverse(G(B)) is differentiable at A. Two more applications of DifferentiableAt.clm_comp show that F(B) = B ∘ (Ring.inverse(G(B)) ∘ adj(B)) is differentiable at A.
6. (Conclusion.) By steps 3 and 4, Πr and F agree on the neighbourhood S of A, i.e. Πr =ᶠ[𝓝 A] F. A map that agrees near A with a map differentiable at A is differentiable at A (DifferentiableAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq). Hence B ↦ (LinearMap.range B.toLinearMap).starProjection is differentiable at A. ∎
key_steps: B ↦ B* is a continuous real-linear map, hence differentiable.
A injective ⇒ the Gram operator A*A is injective, hence a unit of L(ℝⁿ, ℝⁿ).
Units form an open set, so S = {B : B*B is a unit} is a neighbourhood of A.
On S, (range B).starProjection = B (B*B)⁻¹ B*, by the orthogonality characterisation of the projection.
B ↦ B (B*B)⁻¹ B* is differentiable at A (clm_comp, and differentiability of Ring.inverse at units).
Agreement on a neighbourhood transfers differentiability to the range projection.
